Class SocketClientHandler

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.am02.server.network.socket.SocketClientHandler
All Implemented Interfaces:
VirtualView, ClientHandler
public class SocketClientHandler extends Object implements ClientHandler
Server-side handler for a single Socket-connected client.

Inbound: a reader loop deserializes JSON lines into Command records and dispatches them via dispatch(Command), implementing the Inversion of Control pattern symmetrically to Event.apply(VirtualView) on the client side. Command records are used solely as the deserialization target; they are never passed downstream.

Outbound: each VirtualView notification constructs the corresponding Event record, enqueues it, and returns immediately. A dedicated writer thread drains the queue and serializes events to the socket, so GameController never blocks on I/O while holding its lock.

Keep-alive — bidirectional ping-pong: liveness is checked in both directions over the same TCP stream, mirroring the two independent RMI ping() calls used in the RMI transport.

  • Server → client: a ScheduledExecutorService enqueues a PingEvent every 5 seconds. The client replies with a PongCommand, which resets lastPongReceivedAt in dispatch(Command). If no PongCommand is received within 10 seconds, disconnect() is called.
  • Client → server: the client sends periodic PingCommands; dispatch(Command) intercepts them and enqueues a PongEvent in reply. No controller involvement is required for either direction.

    • SocketClientHandler

      public SocketClientHandler(Socket socket, it.polimi.ingsw.am02.common.serialization.JsonMessageCodec codec) throws IOException
      Creates a handler for the given socket, registers it with ControllerManager, and initializes the outbound event queue and ping scheduler.
      Parameters:
      socket - the accepted client socket
      codec - the codec used to serialize Event records and deserialize Command records as newline-delimited JSON
      Throws:
      IOException - if obtaining the socket's output stream fails

  • Method Details

    • listen

      public void listen()
      Starts the outbound writer thread, the ping scheduler, and then enters the blocking reader loop. Returns only when the connection is closed.

      Must be called from a dedicated thread, as the reader loop blocks until the socket is closed or an I/O error occurs.
